A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PAUL and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. Inspection includes v1's appendix; its sensitivity analysis is relocated in v2, while its theoretical section is omitted.

before.justification: V1 reports original GTA-UAV and UAV-VisLoc experiments, component ablations, visual case studies, and appendix hyperparameter results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, sensitivity studies, and attention-map examples.

M1.justification: The dual-network architecture, GMM partitioning, EDL masking, exchanged supervision, and losses remain unchanged. Co-divide is renamed Co-partition. Equation 11 explicitly writes the largest-connected-component operation already specified in v1's prose.

E1.justification: Both evaluate synthetic GTA-UAV and reorganized real-world UAV-VisLoc with the same geographical coverage and noise scenarios. The added discussion of ground-satellite benchmarks does not introduce evaluations on them.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 includes InfoNCE, NCR, BiCro, CRCL, CREAM, ESC, GSC, and RCL; Table 2 includes the same comparators except RCL in both versions. Ablation comparators also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, metrics, noise levels, ViT-Base encoder, 384-by-384 inputs, Adam optimizer, five training epochs, batch size 64, and one warmup epoch are unchanged. V2 clarifies the existing sensitivity study's setting without establishing a protocol change.

E4.justification: Component ablations, partition strategies, guidance losses, augmentation variants, and the two visual case studies are retained. Hyperparameter sensitivity moves from v1's appendix Tables 4–5 to v2 Section 4.5.2 and Figures 5–6; it is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained evidential uncertainty concerns model predictions, not statistical uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 are numerically identical, including PAUL's 58.70% GTA-UAV cross-area R@1 and 26.64% UAV-VisLoc R@1 at 30% noise. Corresponding figures retain the same results and examples. The sensitivity charts reproduce the appendix table values, with SDM expressed as percentages.

T1.justification: V2 removes the entire Dempster–Shafer theoretical appendix. V1 defines belief-mass assignments, derives singleton and uncertainty masses in Equations 14–15, verifies normalization, and connects these quantities to Dirichlet predictions. The main mathematical formulation remains, but this supporting derivation has no counterpart in v2.

C1.justification: Both claim a pioneering systematic treatment of NC-CVGL, introduce PAUL to exploit partially aligned noisy pairs through uncertainty learning, and claim superior performance across noise settings. Rewritten contributions and the explicit three-stage summary retain the same scientific scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking noisy positive pairs to disturbed metric margins and residual noise to confirmation bias, motivating evidential regularization. It also explicitly distinguishes UAV-satellite applicability from ground-satellite benchmarks. The principal result interpretations and future real-platform evaluation plans remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.5.2 newly identifies GTA-UAV, the cross-area split, and 30% noise as the setting for the retained hyperparameter sweeps; v1's appendix did not specify this setting. Existing implementation, training, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to CoCa and multimodal entity-linking work, removes the Adam, Shafer, ROS-SAM, and YOLO-core references, and expands UAV-versus-ground research positioning. The main related-work coverage and novelty positioning remain intact; duplicate-reference consolidation is bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, method explanations, and conclusion, introduces numbered sections and subsections, and integrates sensitivity analysis into the main experiments. Terminology, author affiliations, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the opening schematic, separates the noise-degradation plot into Figure 2, revises the pipeline graphic, and converts appendix sensitivity tables into bar charts. Tables are restyled and relocated. Table 2's erroneous GTA-UAV ablation caption is corrected to identify the UAV-VisLoc comparison.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves interpretability by correcting Table 2's misleading caption, specifying the sensitivity study's setting, and explaining the three-stage method more clearly. The core algorithm and empirical evidence remain intact. Removing the supporting Dempster–Shafer derivation and replacing exact sensitivity tables with unlabeled bars reduce accessible detail, limiting the overall gain.
